assumptions: Earliest galaxies at redshift z ~ 4, as used by Martel, Shapiro & Weinberg 1998.
Primordial fluctuation amplitude Q and dark-matter-to-photon ratio held at our values (Tegmark et al. 2006 show the bound scales with Q^3).
Our density ratio Omega_Lambda/Omega_m = 0.685/0.315 (Planck 2018).

Spherical top-hat collapse with the linear growing mode (MSW 1998 eq. 4 and eq. 57); collapse at z = 4 means linear overdensity 1.686 (Einstein-de Sitter value, IMPORTED); Lambda negligible before z = 4.

Applies to positive Lambda. For negative Lambda, structure forms readily in the recollapsing phase (Peacock 2007), so this link PASSes; the negative-Lambda limit is the lifetime link l.s11.lambda-lifetime.
links.notes: Weinberg 1987 and MSW 1998 eq. (4), p.6: a spherical fluctuation recollapses iff rho_V <= (500/729) delta^3 rhobar, with delta the linear growing-mode overdensity at recombination (MSW use the growing-mode sigma, eq. 57). A galaxy at z ~ 4 has linear overdensity 1.686 at z = 4, and delta^3 rhobar is invariant under linear growth, so rho_V <= (500/729) 1.686^3 (1+z)^3 rho_m0 = 411 rho_m0. With Omega_m = 0.315 (Planck 2018) and Omega_Lambda = 0.685, rho_Lambda,ours = 2.17 rho_m0, so the bound is 189 in dial units. Until atlas@locked-2026-11-16a this link used 57.5 = 125/2.17, treating (1+z)^3 rho_m0 = 125 rho_m0 as the bound; MSW p.3 and Weinberg 1996 p.3 state 125 rho_m0 only as a value the bound cannot be much less than (docs/locks/LOCKED_LAMBDA_GALAXY_189.md). MSW also find the observed-typical value is much smaller than this bound. FAIL above the bound; PASS below.

assumptions: The electromagnetic part of the neutron-proton mass difference scales linearly with alpha (leading order).
Quark masses (and so the QCD part Q) are held fixed while alpha changes.
Errors on Q and E are treated as independent 1-sigma intervals.
links.notes: m_n - m_p = Q + E*(alpha/alpha0), Q = 2.52 +/- 0.29 MeV (QCD), E = -1.00 +/- 0.16 MeV (QED) (Borsanyi et al. 2015). Hydrogen is stable against electron capture iff m_n - m_p > m_e = beta * 938.272 MeV. PASS if stable over the whole 1-sigma box, FAIL if unstable over all of it, else CONTESTED. At beta = ours the central critical alpha is 2.01 x ours (0.01466); band 1.48-2.73 x ours.

assumptions: The Coulomb coefficient a_c scales linearly with alpha and the surface coefficient a_s scales linearly with the strong-force change s; all other nuclear structure is held fixed.
Liquid-drop coefficients a_s = 17.8 MeV, a_c = 0.711 MeV (one published fit; other fits differ by a few percent).
Nuclei follow the valley-of-stability relation Z = A/2 - 0.2 A^2/(A + 200) (approximation used in derive.py, not separately sourced).

The table ends where spontaneous fission becomes barrier-free (Z^2/A at the Bohr-Wheeler limit) or where the 1s level dives into the Dirac sea (Z ~ 1.24/alpha); shell effects and islands of stability are ignored.
Electron masses and the proton mass are held fixed.
links.notes: Periodic table ends at min(relativistic limit Z ~ 1.24/alpha (Z_cr ~ 170 at our alpha, Zeldovich & Popov 1972), liquid-drop fission limit Z^2/A = 2*a_s*(1+s)/(a_c*alpha/alpha0) (Bohr & Wheeler 1939), with a_s = 17.8 MeV and a_c = 0.711 MeV (Rohlf 1994 fit)). PASS end >= 26 (iron); WEAK 8 <= end < 26 (C and O exist, heavier missing); FAIL end < 8. Z_fission(alpha, strong) = largest Z with Z^2/A(Z) below that limit, A(Z) from the valley-of-stability approximation in derive.py. Ours: relativistic 137 (Dirac) to 169 (finite nucleus), fission 134. links.label: CONTESTED
assumptions: Spatially flat universe dominated by matter after early times; radiation ignored. The lifetime then depends only on |Lambda|.
Observers need at least as long as they took here (13.787 Gyr, Planck 2018). This is a one-sample benchmark, not a derived requirement.
The heating-to-8 K cutoff that Peacock 2007 discusses is not modelled.
links.notes: Negative Lambda makes a flat universe recollapse. Its total lifetime is t = (2*pi/3)/H_L with H_L = sqrt(8*pi*G*|rho_Lambda|/3), exact for flat matter + Lambda < 0 (derive.d11). With Planck 2018 H0 = 67.4 km/s/Mpc and Omega_Lambda = 0.685, t = 36.7 Gyr / sqrt(|x|) for dial value x < 0. The anthropic condition for negative Lambda is that the universe survives long enough for observers (Barrow & Tipler 1986, as stated by Martel, Shapiro & Weinberg 1998). The literature gives no agreed lifetime threshold: Peacock 2007 finds that structure forms readily while recollapsing, and that negative Lambda is disfavoured only if observers cannot form once the recollapsing universe heats above 8 K. The condition shown uses our own single sample as the benchmark (observers at 13.787 Gyr, Planck 2018), giving x >= -7.09. With a 5 Gyr benchmark it would be x >= -53.9. CONTESTED because the threshold is an assumption, not a result. PASS for every positive Lambda.

crosslinks.label: CONJECTURE
crosslinks.a_pattern: Uncatalysed hydrolysis of labile biological phosphoanhydrides in dilute solution, especially Mg·ATP, with published k(25 °C) and ΔH‡ that can be Eyring-extrapolated to 122 °C (Stockbridge and Wolfenden 2009).
crosslinks.b_pattern: Doubling time of a recorded high-temperature organism, Methanopyrus kandleri 116, at 122 °C and 20 MPa (Takai 2008).
crosslinks.connection: At 122 °C, uncatalysed Mg·ATP²⁻ hydrolysis (t½ ≈ 6 min, Stockbridge & Wolfenden 2009, Eyring-extrapolated 12 °C beyond their 50–110 °C data) decays about 125× faster than M. kandleri 116 doubles (~12 h, Takai 2008 Fig. 2A, digitised). Ratio t½/t_d: median 0.0079, 90% interval 0.0050–0.0127 (79–200× faster); P(more than 100× faster, the lock's kill edge) ≈ 0.79 (Monte Carlo, Mathematician, docs/analysis/chg2_mc.py; 0.65–0.92 across sweeps). The uncertainty is dominated by the growth rate, which Takai estimated from only 3–4 points. If life's ceiling is not set by this bond, cells must outrun its decay by upkeep. That reading is suggested, not shown. Fragile: ATP⁴⁻ or Mg·ADP as the species (ratio 0.08 / 0.05), the Fig. 1B growth rate (P ≈ 0.96), or the other 122 °C point (P ≈ 1.0) each change the picture. Rates were measured in dilute solution.
crosslinks.breaks_if: With the locked comparison at 122 °C / 20 MPa, t_min/t_d falls in the strict window [0.01, 100] (lability ceiling coincides with life's ceiling), or t_min > 100 t_d (bonds outlast the cell, so the ceiling is set by something else). The species was not fixed in the lock: substituting ATP4- or Mg·ADP would already move the present numbers inside that window, which is why the label stays short of a stronger grade.
crosslinks.notes: CH-G2 / inbox #17. Lock 97c6394, scorer correction 9ab566e (Amendment 1 clause 3: the 100× window is not loosened to 200×). Chemist checked the digitisation and agrees. Verdict KILLED on the 'life outruns uncatalysed decay by upkeep' branch: t_min/t_d = 0.0080, about 125×. The overall label is CONJECTURE because the hydrolysed species was not fixed in the lock and rates were measured in dilute solution. Wolfenden 2011 was not opened; numbers come from opened full texts of papers it cites. The connection was reworded in the 2026-11-20 reanalysis; it is not the locked card text quoted in results-2026-11-19.md. Mathematician MC (2026-11-20, not a locked test; docs/analysis/chg2_mc.py): pivoting the Arrhenius fit at its 77.5 °C data centre, dH‡ ±0.2 kcal/mol (Table 2 footnote: errors ≤0.4), ln k(pivot) ±0.10, ln μ ±0.25, T ±1 K. Half-life run: P(<0.01)=0.79, median 0.0079, 90% [0.0050, 0.0127]. Mean-lifetime run (τ=1/k vs t_d): P=0.32, median 0.0114, 90% [0.0072, 0.0182]. τ vs t_d mixes conventions; τ vs 1/μ equals the half-life ratio. The locked point verdict KILLED stands; the probability shows it is likely but not robust.

crosslinks.label: ANALOGY-ONLY
crosslinks.a_pattern: Gel effect / Norrish-Trommsdorff autoacceleration: in a free-radical polymerization, termination is diffusion-limited. As conversion rises, so does viscosity; termination then slows more than propagation, the radical population grows, and the rate and the heat output run away. This is a runaway that starts when a brake weakens. It has no inverted-U optimum.
crosslinks.b_pattern: Security dilemma: one state arms, or otherwise builds up, in order to feel safer. Its neighbour reads that move as a threat and arms too. Both end up less safe than before. In Jervis's account the dilemma is strongest when offence has the advantage and offensive and defensive arms are indistinguishable.
crosslinks.connection: These rows share a verbal pattern, not a shared derivation: a control meant to restrain something ends up increasing it, or otherwise defeating the aim. No common model is claimed. The gel effect and the security dilemma are both positive feedback triggered by a safety step; that parallel is an analogy unless it is written as one reaction-equation model. Two further rows of the same verbal pattern are recorded in notes: the 1902 Hanoi rat bounty (metric gaming) and contested risk compensation (Peltzman 1975).
crosslinks.breaks_if: Not breakable as a cause, because it claims none. It is retired if the negative analogy grows to cover the positive one, or upgraded only if someone writes a common model that makes a locked, distinctive prediction and that prediction holds.
crosslinks.notes: Card-level claim is ANALOGY-ONLY (verbal pattern only; no common model). History rows (security dilemma; Hanoi 1902): Historian. The gel effect was removed from the inverted-U / w-curve pattern and belongs here as its own row; linking it to the w-curve stays an analogy until someone shows the two come from the same equation. Brennan, Lo and Zhao is not a row on this card. The Delhi cobra-bounty story is an unverified legend and is not a row. Goodhart 1975 is named only as a pattern label for metric gaming; no Crossref DOI was confirmed, so it is not a source entry. Row 1, gel effect: ESTABLISHED; evidence_rung 2 (produced and suppressed by experimental intervention: Norrish & Smith 1942; Trommsdorff, Kohle & Lagally 1948; O'Neil, Wisnudel & Torkelson 1996); not rung 3, because no prediction from a named kinetic model has been locked in this atlas and held on unseen data; model_exists true (O'Neil & Torkelson 1999; Achilias 2007). Row 2, security dilemma: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS (mainstream IR theory; case fit is contested and is not treated as establishing the mechanism); evidence_rung 1; model_exists true as a verbal strategic model (Jervis 1978); no simulation or quantitative model is cited here, and none has been locked against a pre-declared case set, so the flag does not raise the rung. Row 3, Hanoi rat bounty 1902: ESTABLISHED as an episode (the tail bounty, the cutting and release of rats, and the dropping of the bounty); farming is reported, its scale is uncertain and is not treated as a measured fact; evidence_rung 1 (Vann 2003 is a historical reconstruction, not an intervention designed to test a locked model); model_exists false for this episode; Campbell 1979 names the broader metric-gaming pattern and is not a model of Hanoi. Row 4, risk compensation: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS, contested; evidence_rung 1 (the 1975 design could be read as a natural experiment, but the causal reading is disputed, so the row is not raised to rung 2); model_exists true (Peltzman 1975); no later critique is cited, because none was Crossref-checked for this card. Two proposed lockable tests (not scored): T1, O'Neil & Torkelson 1999 on an unseen polymerization series, aimed at raising row 1 toward rung 3; T2, Jervis's offence-defence claim on an unseen set of rivalries that excludes the Anglo-German naval race. A re-lock after seeing the numbers, or that reuses the same series or cases with a new measure picked after the result, would be a rescue. A single reaction-equation model covering row 1 and row 2 is not proposed as a test here.

crosslinks.label: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS
crosslinks.a_pattern: Volcanology/climate: a cluster of large eruptions in 536, 540 and 547 CE (re-dated ice cores, Sigl et al. 2015); the 536/540 'double event' gave the largest decadal NH extratropical radiative forcing in 1,200 years and simulated NH mean cooling of more than 2 C at peak (Toohey et al. 2016).
crosslinks.b_pattern: History: an unprecedented, long, synchronized cooling from 536 to about 660 CE, named the Late Antique Little Ice Age, proposed as an additional factor in the Justinian plague, the transformation of the eastern Roman Empire, the collapse of the Sasanian Empire, steppe and Arabian migrations and upheavals in China (Buentgen et al. 2016).
crosslinks.connection: Sulfate forcing -> multi-year cooling, prolonged by ocean and sea-ice feedbacks and a solar minimum (Buentgen et al. 2016) -> high likelihood of multiple years of significant crop losses, e.g. in Scandinavia (Toohey et al. 2016) -> famine and stress on states.
crosslinks.breaks_if: Independent tree-ring networks show no NH summer cooling in 536-545 beyond normal variability. Societal events attributed to the LALIA are shown to start before 536, or to be equally frequent in comparable unforced centuries. Dated grain or settlement evidence for Scandinavia shows no decline in the decade after 536/540.
crosslinks.notes: Crop losses are a model-based mainstream hypothesis (Toohey et al. 2016). The plague and empire outcomes remain contested; Büntgen et al. 2016 themselves call the cooling an 'additional environmental factor'.

crosslinks.label: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS
crosslinks.a_pattern: Volcanology: the c.1257 ice-core sulfate spike (largest volcanic sulfur release to the stratosphere in the past 7,000 years) comes from Samalas, Lombok; eruption between May and October 1257, column up to 43 km, at least 40 km3 DRE (Lavigne et al. 2013).
crosslinks.b_pattern: History: the English food crisis of 1258, with bad weather, failed harvests, famine refugees in London and mass graves at St Mary Spital (Campbell 2017).
crosslinks.connection: Stratospheric sulfate -> cooling and unstable weather -> harvest failure -> famine. Lavigne et al. report that tree rings, medieval chronicles and models corroborate worldwide climatic effects.
crosslinks.breaks_if: Documentary price and harvest records show the English harvest failure starting before any climatic effect of a May-October 1257 eruption could arrive (i.e. the 1256 or early-1257 harvests already failed at crisis level). High-resolution proxies attribute the 1257-58 weather anomaly to solar forcing, with no volcanic cooling signal in England's growing season.
crosslinks.notes: The 1258 English famine step is contested: Campbell 2017 weighs Samalas against strong solar forcing and says the answer depends on the precise chronology. Lavigne et al. 2013 report that tree rings, medieval chronicles and models corroborate the climatic effects.

crosslinks.label: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS
crosslinks.a_pattern: Physics/climate: the April 1815 Tambora eruption injected about 28 Tg of sulfur into the stratosphere (eVolv2k ice-core composite, Toohey & Sigl 2017, ~16% uncertainty), about 3x Pinatubo 1991 (9 +/- 2 Tg S, Guo et al. 2004). Oppenheimer 2003 gave ~60 Tg S ('six times Pinatubo'); the newer value is about half that.
crosslinks.b_pattern: Biology/history: 1816, the 'Year without a summer', brought anomalously cold weather to the northeastern USA, maritime Canada and Europe; crop failures were widespread (Oppenheimer 2003). Severe famine in Switzerland, one of the worst-hit regions (Bronnimann & Kramer 2016, preface).
crosslinks.connection: Sulfate aerosol veil -> reduced shortwave at the surface -> Northern Hemisphere cooling, well constrained by proxies, with no strong Southern Hemisphere signal (Raible et al. 2016) -> cold, wet growing season -> harvest failure -> famine and price shocks.
crosslinks.breaks_if: Re-dated ice cores place the c.1815-16 sulfate peak on a different eruption, or show stratospheric loading far below the cited ~28 Tg S. Early instrumental and proxy series show no 1816 summer anomaly in Western Europe / NE North America beyond normal year-to-year spread. Harvest and grain-price series for the affected regions show no 1816-17 anomaly, or an equal anomaly in unaffected regions. Social step only: emigration or typhus rises start before the harvest failure, or are equally strong in regions without the cold anomaly. A dated proxy/instrumental NH summer series where 1816 is within 2 sigma of interannual noise.
crosslinks.notes: Kept as one record through to typhus, so the overall label is the weakest step (MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS). Oppenheimer describes emigration and typhus as 'implicated in' the aftermath, not as a demonstrated consequence. Full text of Brönnimann & Krämer 2016 (Geographica Bernensia G90, 48 pp.) was read from the Internet Archive copy of boris.unibe.ch/81880/1/tambora_e_A4l.pdf; the live BORIS portal returned an empty file. Step 3 (harvest failure -> famine) is supported on p. 11: 'the cold and rainy summers indeed led to poor harvests, which was one of the factors causing famine and the last subsistence crisis of the western world.'; p. 7: 'The reduction in harvest yield in Europe contributed to the "last great subsistence crisis in the western world,"'; p. 3 (preface): 'Switzerland was among the most severely affected regions: severe famine cost countless lives'; p. 28 records failed 1816 harvests setting off price inflation, while noting that 'the poor harvest was not the only reason for the crisis.'; pp. 32-33 treat the 1816-17 famine in Switzerland (thefts, mortality, baptisms; a 'true famine' in the east). Oppenheimer 2003 was not used as a full-text check for the famine step. Sulfur loading in pattern a updated from Oppenheimer 2003 (~60 Mt S) to 28.1 Tg S (eVolv2k, Toohey & Sigl 2017, 16% uncertainty); Guo et al. 2004 give Pinatubo as 9 +/- 2 Tg S (18 +/- 4 Mt SO2). Step stratospheric sulfate -> 1816 cooling quantitative check (Physicist forge 2026-11-19, lock f43523b): N-TREND (Wilson et al. 2016) NH extratropical May-Aug: 1816 is -0.66 K vs 1810-14, 3.7x interannual noise. Scaling note: Tambora/Pinatubo cooling ratio 2.0 vs sulfur ratio 3.1: cooling grows slower than sulfur (closer to M^(2/3), aerosol particle growth). Preference fragile to Pinatubo's sulfur uncertainty.

crosslinks.label: CONJECTURE
crosslinks.a_pattern: A country-relative modernization clock: a person's birth year measured from the year their own country crossed a development threshold (internet users >= 50%, mobile subscriptions >= 50 per 100, GDP per capita >= 10,000 2011 int$, or gross secondary enrollment >= 50%).
crosslinks.b_pattern: Worldview as measured by six Integrated Values Surveys items, 1981-2022 (trust A165, importance of God F063, post-materialism Y002, left-right E033, justifiability of homosexuality F118, happiness A008), across birth cohorts born 1940-2005.
crosslinks.connection: Tested Sajjad's TOE-room hypothesis (2026-11-22) that when a person was born best predicts how they see reality. What was tested is worldview as measured by the six IVS items above, not perception. Cohort as the best predictor: KILLED (Historian lock fff88a0, Part A: calendar birth cohort ranked last of four blocks in 5/6 items; country dominated, 57-85% of the partial R2). Calendar year versus a country-relative clock: the internet clock (T50) beat calendar cohort by dBIC <= -10 in 4/6 items (A165 -106.9, F063 -669.8, E033 -146.1, A008 -339.3; calendar won Y002 +48.8 and F118 +103.7). Which clock it is: NOT-TESTABLE-YET on open data (Historian lock ab1fe35: internet won 3/6, income 1/6, 2 ties, on 12 middle-income countries with a clean year on all four clocks). In an unscored check after the verdict, income fit best: on raw fit (-2 log L) income was best on 5/6 items and schooling on A165; internet's BIC wins came from the parameter penalty. That check is post hoc and is not a verdict.
crosslinks.breaks_if: A new pre-registered test on a larger common sample (or the CHAT technology dataset, not yet used) in which calendar birth cohort beats every country-relative clock by dBIC <= -10 in >= 4 of 6 items would break the 'clock beats calendar' half. 'Which clock' needs a sample where one clock wins >= 4 of 6; income winning would make it REDUCES-TO-KNOWN (Inglehart modernization), internet winning would be new.
crosslinks.notes: Locks: Historian fff88a0 (birth cohort vs technology) and ab1fe35 (which clock), both on branch historian-locks-1 of this repo (not merged to main). Scores (Physicist forge): 2026-11-22-cohort-tech-score commit 25a0089 (Part A KILLED; Part B TECH 4/6, so the technology branch SURVIVED and the calendar branch KILLED under fff88a0 section 5) and 2026-11-23-cohort-clocks-score commit 7e52619 (NOT-TESTABLE-YET). Knife edge in ab1fe35: A008 internet-vs-mobile gap -9.9994 misses the <= -10 rule by 0.0006 BIC; applied as written, it is a tie. In fff88a0 Part B about 64 of each dBIC is BIC's parameter penalty (M_tech has 5 fewer effective parameters); on fit alone tech still wins the same 4/6 items (post-outcome diagnostic). Caveats: rests on ASSUMED common age effects and survey-year fixed effects; Part B uses the 71-77 countries that crossed 50% internet by their last survey, mostly richer ones; with mobile phones as the clock there is no winner (3/3). Data: WVS Trend v4.1 file (the DOI record lists version 4.0) stacked with EVS ZA7503 v3.0.0; World Bank IT.NET.USER.ZS, IT.CEL.SETS.P2, SE.SEC.ENRR; Maddison 2023. Inglehart and Baker 2000 is the seen rival (modernization). Rung 1: an association in survey data; neither lock made a directional prediction that held.

crosslinks.label: CONJECTURE
crosslinks.a_pattern: Upper-tail city growth over 2010-2020 is size-independent (Gibrat's law: regression slope b of decade log-growth on log 2010 size is near 0).
crosslinks.b_pattern: The same country's 2020 city-size distribution is Zipf (rank-size exponent alpha near 1).
crosslinks.connection: Hypothesis (Gabaix 1999): in real urban systems, proportional growth in the upper tail plus some force that keeps small cities from vanishing produces Zipf's law. The model identity is x.math.gibrat-floor-zipf. This record is the claim that it is the actual mechanism in real countries. Country-level test status: forge Claim E (lock e3bc861, WUP 2025 F21) was KILLED 17 vs threshold 16, using 'CI contains the null' as 'holds'. A post-hoc bootstrap TOST reanalysis (90% percentile CI, Zipf margin [0.9, 1.1], Gibrat margin |b| <= 0.01) finds Zipf equivalent in 3/74 countries (CHN, IND, RUS), non-equivalent in 7, and inconclusive in 64. Gibrat is equivalent in 0/64, non-equivalent in 14, and inconclusive in 50. Only one country is decisive for E: CHN, where Zipf is equivalent but Gibrat is clearly non-equivalent (b = +0.051, big cities growing faster). The data cannot confirm or kill E at country level.
crosslinks.breaks_if: Under a new pre-registered lock with an equivalence test: at least max(5, 25% of decisive units) countries where Zipf is equivalent to 1 and Gibrat is non-equivalent, or the reverse, or a pooled or hierarchical estimate showing upper-tail growth that depends on size while Zipf holds.
crosslinks.notes: Split from x.hist.zipf-gibrat (real-city half). Label CONJECTURE, not MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS. The atlas's own data neither supports nor kills the explanation, and the only decisive country (CHN) runs against it. The TOST was written after the forge results were seen, so it is a reanalysis, not a locked verdict: the forge E verdict under its lock stands as recorded, with the caveat that it rests on treating non-rejection as acceptance. Power: the Hill 90% interval half-width is about 1.645*alpha/sqrt(n), so equivalence at +/-0.1 needs roughly 270+ cities above 50k. Most countries have fewer, so country-level equivalence is structurally unreachable. Robustness at a 100k cutoff: N_Z 51 (0 EQUIV, 7 NONEQUIV, 44 INCONCL), no decisive E units. Code docs/analysis/zipf_tost.py. WUP values are DEGURBA model estimates (IMPORTED caveat from the forge run).

crosslinks.label: CONJECTURE
crosslinks.a_pattern: Elemental rank order in the solar photosphere (Asplund, Amarsi and Grevesse 2021, Table 2), compared with the continental crust as a rival ranking (Rudnick and Gao 2003, Table 3).
crosslinks.b_pattern: Elemental rank order in a whole organism. No E. coli table covering at least 15 of the 20 locked elements was found, so the lock's fallback is ICRP Publication 23 (1975) Reference Man, Table 110.
crosslinks.connection: The rank order of elements in the body (ICRP 23 Reference Man) tracks the Sun (Asplund 2021; ρ = 0.65) far better than the crust (Rudnick & Gao 2003; ρ = 0.05). With H and C dropped, the Sun still leads, 0.52 vs 0.41. A rank correlation cannot separate cosmic availability from chemistry and stars favouring the same light elements.
crosslinks.breaks_if: On the locked 20-element set, Spearman ρ between body ranks and crust ranks is greater than or equal to ρ with the Sun, or ρ with the Sun falls below 0.5.
crosslinks.notes: CH-G3 / inbox #18. Lock 97c6394, results 92a0999. Verdict SURVIVED (ρ_S = 0.651, ρ_C = 0.054, atom-number basis). Label CONJECTURE, evidence_rung 1, as in the card: a rank correlation cannot separate cosmic availability from chemistry and stars favouring the same light elements. Asplund 2021 doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202140445 was Crossref-verified; numbers were taken from the arXiv full text (2105.01661). Rudnick and Gao 2003 doi:10.1016/b0-08-043751-6/03016-4 was Crossref-verified as the 2003 Treatise on Geochemistry chapter (pp. 1-64); the publisher text was not opened, and crust values were read from a third-party copy (flagged). ICRP 23 (1975) Table 110 was opened as full text by the scorer; no Crossref work DOI for the 1975 report itself was found, only later notices and reviews, which are not used as the source and are not in sources/. Card text used verbatim as the connection.

crosslinks.label: ESTABLISHED
crosslinks.a_pattern: Logically irreversible erasure of one bit in a system at temperature T dissipates at least k_B T ln 2 of heat (0.018 eV at 300 K).
crosslinks.b_pattern: A cell that resets a stored internal state (for example a receptor that forgets its last reading so it can sense again) must dissipate at least that bound per bit erased.
crosslinks.connection: Same physical process in both systems: the second law applied to a many-to-one map on a memory register. Landauer derived the bound; Berut et al. measured it with a colloidal bit; Mehta and Schwab apply the same thermodynamics to a cellular sensing network.
crosslinks.breaks_if: A measured erasure, in any carrier, dissipating reliably less than k_B T ln 2 per bit with the full environment accounted for.
crosslinks.notes: ESTABLISHED as a lower bound: erasure causes at least this heat. Cell-side split: (a) 'Cell computation is bounded below by kT ln2 per bit erased' is evidence_rung 3 (a universal inequality, Landauer 1961, confirmed experimentally by Berut et al. 2012, so it applies to cells as a bound) and is the second chain step. (b) 'Cells operate near that bound' / 'cells work near the bound' is evidence_rung 0, with model_exists true and model_refs Mehta & Schwab 2012, and with no measured case. (b) is not claimed and is therefore not a chain step: putting it in the chain would force the overall evidence_rung to 0 and the overall label off ESTABLISHED, understating the bound that is the actual claim. Neural signalling dissipates ≥10^5× kT ln2 per bit transmitted (Laughlin 1998). This is not an erasure measurement, so it does not bear on whether cells work near Landauer's bound. Atlas link l.s10.landauer carries the physics side.

crosslinks.label: CONJECTURE
crosslinks.a_pattern: Eigen's error threshold: a sequence persists only if the per-copy information loss stays below a line set by the master's selective superiority, U = e×L < ln(σ) (Eigen 1971). At the T-B1 assumed σ=100, the line is 4.6 (NEAR band to 9.2).
crosslinks.b_pattern: Published RNA-catalysed, template-directed RNA polymerase or replicase ribozymes, scored by overall per-nucleotide error rate e on a real template and by the full length L of the assayed construct.
crosslinks.connection: The most accurate published polymerase ribozyme (Johnston 2001 R18, e≈0.011 from Sanger reads on a mixed 11-nt template, 196 nt) is below Eigen's error threshold for its own length at an assumed σ=100 (e×L≈2.2 < 4.6; 95% CI 1.1–3.7). Caveats: (1) on the paper's Table 2 single-base average it would be NEAR (6.5); (2) fidelity was measured on short templates, and no ribozyme has copied its own ~200-nt folded sequence (missing experiment); (3) at σ=10 only R18 is below the line; (4) the verdict is decided by the best ribozyme, and newer, more processive ones (2026 preprint) are above threshold. Rung 1, model flag.
crosslinks.breaks_if: Under the T-B1 lock (3e54e77), the qualifying ribozyme with the lowest e is ABOVE the threshold (e×L ≥ 9.2 at σ=100), or a later measurement of that ribozyme copying its own full, folded construct yields e×L ≥ 9.2. Finding that the paper's Table 2 single-base average is the only reported overall e would have made the primary NEAR, not a kill by itself.
crosslinks.notes: Later T-B1 card wording, used verbatim as the connection. Lock 3e54e77, screen d551d86, score c1cc472. Verdict SURVIVED on the lock's primary (Johnston 2001 R18, Sanger mixed 11-nt template). REDUCES-TO-KNOWN is not a verdict line for this test. The overall label is CONJECTURE because 'below threshold for its own length' is an extrapolation: fidelity was measured on short templates, and no ribozyme has copied its own ~200-nt folded sequence (missing experiment). Eigen's relation is ESTABLISHED theory and is the model (model_exists, model_refs eigen1971); it does not raise the real-system rung. The 2026 preprint (Horning, Nasser and Joyce, doi:10.64898/2026.10.18.759947, Crossref-verified posted-content) is the secondary most-recent line and is ABOVE; it does not change the primary verdict. Lab models of early Earth, not evidence from it.

crosslinks.label: CONJECTURE
crosslinks.a_pattern: Standard big-bang nucleosynthesis with the CMB baryon density predicts a primordial lithium-7 abundance 7Li/H = 5.53e-10 (the SBBN value used by Ovchynnikov 2026).
crosslinks.b_pattern: The lithium abundance measured spectroscopically in the atmospheres of old, metal-poor stars is lower: 1.45e-10 (the Particle Data Group value used by Ovchynnikov 2026), a factor 5.53/1.45 = 3.81.
crosslinks.connection: The gap (the cosmological lithium problem) is open, with two rival explanations that act at different times. (1) Decaying relics, before stars form: relics with lifetimes of a few hours, decaying mostly into ~100 MeV electron antineutrinos plus e+-/photons, turn protons into neutrons that destroy 7Be, and later EM cascades break up the extra deuterium; the paper's Table I rows end at 7Li/H = 1.5 to 2.3e-10 while keeping D/H, YP and Neff in range (Ovchynnikov 2026; forge check REDUCES-TO-KNOWN, standard BBN plus EM-cascade physics). (2) Stellar depletion, inside stars: atomic diffusion with turbulent mixing carries lithium below the visible atmosphere, so old stars show less than they were born with; Korn et al. 2006 report abundance trends with evolutionary stage in the metal-poor globular cluster NGC 6397 that diffusion models reproduce. Neither rival is established here.
crosslinks.breaks_if: For relics: a Neff shift absent at Simons Observatory precision where the paper's rows predict up to +0.106 (about 2.4 sigma at sigma(Neff) = 0.045), or 6Li/7Li limits that exclude the particle rows (the paper's own 5-17% is already above stellar limits). For stellar depletion: lithium abundances in unevolved metal-poor stars that show no trend with evolutionary stage where diffusion models predict one. If stellar depletion fully closes the gap, no relic is needed; if the measured stellar values are confirmed as primordial, the relic reading gains ground.
crosslinks.notes: Forge run 2026-11-23-0100-lithium-relics (Physicist; lock 55b1252, results f099ddf): verdict REDUCES-TO-KNOWN. P1 SURVIVED (cascade cutoff reaches the D threshold at T = 5.34 keV, t = 4.64e4 s, 0.93 x the paper's 5e4 s); P2 SURVIVED indirect (neutron-driven Li lowering costs >= 30% of the final D/H, which cascades must remove); P3a KILLED on wording only ('about three times' vs 3.81); P3b SURVIVED (2 of 4 Q-ball rows reach <= 1.95e-10); P3c SURVIVED (max |dNeff| 0.106 / 0.045 = 2.36); P4 SURVIVED (lifetimes 2.25-3.44 h). Stellar depletion added as a rival on Physicist's request from the TOE room (2026-11-23). Korn et al. 2006 (Nature 442, 657-659; doi:10.1038/nature05011) checked against Crossref and the arXiv abstract (astro-ph/0608201): they conclude diffusion is 'predominantly responsible' for the low stellar lithium; their abstract gives the discrepancy as a factor two to three, against 3.81 on the paper's newer numbers. Ovchynnikov 2026 checked on arXiv (2611.26691v1, no journal reference yet). Field b is chemistry because the measured quantity is an element abundance; the record links physics to the atlas's s04 to s05 (nuclei and light elements) input without changing any stage link. Nothing in PRR predicts or constrains this. Rung 1: observed trends, no intervention.

crosslinks.label: ESTABLISHED
crosslinks.a_pattern: Reflected multiplicative random growth: a size S with dS/S = mu dt + sigma dB (mu < 0 for normalised sizes) that is reflected at a floor S_min has a Pareto stationary law, P(S > s) = (s/S_min)^(-zeta).
crosslinks.b_pattern: City-size model: if normalised city sizes grow by Gibrat's law (growth independent of size) and are kept above a floor S_min, the steady-state rank-size distribution is Zipf-like with exponent zeta = 1/(1 - S_min/S_bar), where S_bar is the mean normalised size; zeta -> 1 as S_min/S_bar -> 0.
crosslinks.connection: Same mathematics: Gabaix 1999, Proposition 1 (p. 749). The log-size is a reflected Brownian motion with an exponential stationary law, so the size law is Pareto; the condition E[S] = S_bar fixes zeta = 1/(1 - S_min/S_bar). Gibrat's law alone, with no floor, has no steady state: sizes go lognormal with growing variance. Simon 1955 gives the discrete proportional-growth version of the same class. This is a theorem about the model. It says nothing about whether real cities follow it.
crosslinks.breaks_if: An error in the proof of Gabaix 1999 Proposition 1, i.e. a reflected geometric Brownian motion with E[S] = S_bar whose stationary tail exponent is not 1/(1 - S_min/S_bar). A numerical check (Mathematician audit-1, docs/analysis/audit1_zipf_numerology.py Z3) gives Hill(top 500) 1.40 vs 1.43 theory at S_min/S_bar = 0.3 and 1.03 vs 1.11 at 0.1. The 0.02 run did not equilibrate (0.83 vs 1.02), so it is not counted.
crosslinks.notes: Split from x.hist.zipf-gibrat (mathematics half). Gabaix's own footnote 30 warns that the formula is not suitable for estimating real exponents, because zeta varies with city size. Use it only as the model identity. The real-city question is x.hist.gibrat-explains-zipf. evidence_rung 0 because this link makes no claim about a real system; model_exists true.

crosslinks.label: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS
crosslinks.a_pattern: Unpredictable geophysical disaster, especially a large earthquake whose timing is not chosen by the people whose religiosity is later measured. The 22 February 2011 Christchurch earthquake (Mw 6.3) is one such event; geological earthquake risk and the timing of recent nearby quakes are others.
crosslinks.b_pattern: Religiosity and religious affiliation as an outcome: people turning to religious faith to cope with shocks they cannot predict or prevent ('religious coping' / comfort).
crosslinks.connection: People turn to religious faith to cope with shocks they cannot predict or prevent. Geological timing is not chosen by the people whose faith is measured. Sibley and Bulbulia 2012 (full text): NZAVS 2009 and 2011 waves, with the 22 February 2011 Christchurch earthquake (Mw 6.3) in between. Countrywide, net religious affiliation fell about 0.9% over two years (converts 214 / 5.7%, apostates 248 / 6.6%; Table 1). In Canterbury, converts 43 (8.6%) and apostates 26 (5.2%) in a regional n of 501, a net rise of 3.4%. Difference in change by region: chi-squared(3, N = 3740) = 12.39, p = .006. A parallel pattern holds for those who said they were personally affected. No evidence that having faith buffered subjective health; among the earthquake-affected, loss of faith went with health declines. Bentzen figures below are from the 6 September 2018 author PDF (working paper); the typeset Economic Journal 2019 pages were not opened, so those numbers may have been revised in print. A one-standard-deviation rise in earthquake risk is associated with an 8-11% of a standard deviation rise in religiosity (about 80% of the gender gap in religiosity, as stated there). Recent nearby quakes also raise religiosity; the effect fades with time but appears in children of immigrants. Volcanoes and tsunamis go the same way; more predictable storms do not. Coping is the author's preferred channel; mutual insurance and migration 'cannot be ruled out entirely' (published abstract, Crossref, same wording).
crosslinks.breaks_if: In a pre-registered panel whose pre-disaster wave is fixed before an unpredictable geophysical shock, religiosity does not rise in the affected region relative to comparison regions, or Bentzen's association between geological earthquake risk (or recent nearby quakes) and religiosity disappears in a replication that keeps the same identification. Finding that mutual insurance or migration fully accounts for the pattern would undermine the coping mechanism, but would not by itself remove the exogenous timing.
crosslinks.notes: Proposed atlas id l.religion.disaster-coping. Religion is the effect, not the cause. The atlas has no geology field, so the earthquake / unpredictable-disaster side is filed under physics; Bentzen also reports that volcanoes and tsunamis go the same way and that more predictable storms do not. Remaining caveats (insurance, migration, self-reported 'personally affected') do not remove the exogenous timing, so they do not drop the rung to 1, but they keep the label short of ESTABLISHED. This is not a verdict on any faith.

crosslinks.label: CONJECTURE
crosslinks.a_pattern: PRR A1/D2: readings are +1 or -1, and mirrored readings sum to zero. One reading (CONJECTURE) takes +-1 as the phases 0 and pi, the real slice of U(1), so 'mirroring to zero' is destructive interference at phase difference pi.
crosslinks.b_pattern: Network Bell-type experiments with two independent sources exclude real-amplitude quantum theory when independent systems are combined by the tensor product (Renou et al. 2021; Chen et al. 2022; Li et al. 2022).
crosslinks.connection: A REQUIREMENT on PRR, not a PRR prediction. If PRR composes independent systems by the tensor product (ASSUMED; PRR has not stated its composition rule) and its sources are independent, its amplitudes must be complex. Two legs: (1) real amplitudes break local tomography: for two +-1 systems (d=2) a real joint state has 10 parameters but local products span only 9 (10 != 9; normalised 9 vs 8); complex amplitudes give 16 = 4 x 4 (forge H2, code/h2_count.py). (2) Real quantum theory is bounded at T <= 7.66 (7.6605) in the Renou et al. entanglement-swapping test; Chen et al. measured 8.09(1) on superconducting qubits, a 43 standard-deviation violation; Li et al. used a different, tailored inequality on photons (real bound W ~ 0.7486, measured 0.8508 +- 0.0218), a 4.70 standard-deviation violation. Reading +-1 as phases 0 and pi is CONJECTURE.
crosslinks.breaks_if: Under H2-LOCK: any of the three experimental numbers (bound, score or significance) is materially different on re-read, or the explicit rank count disagrees with 10 vs 9. Separately, the requirement stops binding if PRR states a composition rule that is not the tensor product of independent parts (for example a shared extra rebit or an irreducible Peirce-style pairing): Renou et al. note that real quantum theory reproduces any experiment when parts may share arbitrary real states.
crosslinks.notes: Forge verdict REDUCES-TO-KNOWN (H2-LOCK section 5), carried as a requirement on PRR's +-1 to Hilbert-space map, not a prediction; SURVIVED was not an available outcome. Files: docs/forge/2026-11-23-math-h1-h3/ (H2-LOCK.md, code/h2_count.py, out/h2_output.txt; rerun on the box 2026-11-23, byte-identical). Step 2 is the ASSUMED composition rule (tensor product plus independent sources); the crosslink label set has no ASSUMED, so it is carried as CONJECTURE. The overall label is CONJECTURE because steps 1 and 2 are. Citations re-checked 2026-11-23 against Crossref and the arXiv full texts: Renou arXiv:2101.10873 (T <= 7.6605 for real QT; 'T <= 7.66' in the main text); Chen arXiv:2103.08123 (score 8.09(1); 'beats the real-number bound of 7.66 by 43 standard deviations'); Li arXiv:2111.15128 (W_EXP = 0.8508 +- 0.0218 vs W_RQT ~ 0.7486, '4.70 standard deviations'; abstract says 'over 4.5'). Li et al. did not test the 7.66 bound. The step 3 to step 4 order is a reading chain, not a derivation: the experiments exclude real QT directly. Rung 0: no claim about a real system is made for PRR.

crosslinks.label: ANALOGY-ONLY
crosslinks.a_pattern: PRR D5: familiar dimensions, times and physical pictures are readings of one ordered process under different slicings; the prism separates what was already co-defined.
crosslinks.b_pattern: A glass prism separates white light into colours that were already present in it; each colour refracts by a fixed amount (Newton 1672).
crosslinks.connection: None. There is no shared mechanism or shared equation. The resemblance is 'a splitter reveals components that were already there'.
crosslinks.breaks_if: Not breakable as a cause, because it claims none. It is retired if the negative analogy grows to cover the positive one, or upgraded only if someone writes a D5 dispersion relation that predicts a measurable split.
crosslinks.notes: The engine card c.v3o.006.prism-split tests a PROXY mapping whose known mechanism is reaction-diffusion bookkeeping, not optics, so it does not support this link either. The neutral row is where research would start.

crosslinks.label: CONJECTURE
crosslinks.a_pattern: Candidate PRR locality rules that grow a graph from +-1 pairs without putting in a dimension: R1 'born together, with closure' (random 2-tree) and R2 stacked-simplex growth (random Apollonian network). PRR's A1, A2 and D2 do not fix a graph, so only named rules can be tested.
crosslinks.b_pattern: A geometry that looks four-dimensional at large scale has spectral dimension d_s ~ 4 (return probability of a random walk P(sigma) ~ sigma^(-d_s/2) over a scaling window), as in causal dynamical triangulations (Ambjorn, Jurkiewicz and Loll 2005).
crosslinks.connection: None known yet. Forge H3 (Mathematician; lock 218a3a9, outputs a093cf4) measured large-scale d_s with a continuous-time walk at n = 10^5, 3 seeds, band [3.7, 4.3]. R1 (random 2-tree): mean d_s 2.306, KILLED. R2 (random Apollonian): mean d_s 2.600, KILLED. PRR-level: NOT-TESTABLE-YET, because PRR has no locality rule yet. Caveat: both rules make planar graphs by construction, so a result around 2 to 3 says little about higher-dimensional rules. Control R3 (a 4D causal set, which imports d = 4 by hand) gave NO-WINDOW in 3/3 seeds at n = 10^4; it is context only. The instruments passed (Z4 torus 4.125, Z2 torus 2.015).
crosslinks.breaks_if: This is open, not a link. A named PRR locality rule with no dimension put in that gives d_s, both half-window fits, and all 3 seeds inside [3.7, 4.3] at its largest locked size would turn it into a positive (still CONJECTURE that the rule is PRR's). R1 and R2 have already failed that test under H3-LOCK.
crosslinks.notes: Forge verdicts under H3-LOCK section 6: R1 KILLED (n=10^5 seeds d_s 2.147, 2.294, 2.476), R2 KILLED (2.680, 2.540, 2.581), PRR-level NOT-TESTABLE-YET. At n=10^4, R2 seeds 2 and 3 were SATURATED. The runner prints 'RULE R3: KILLED -- NO-WINDOW in 3/3 seeds'; R3 is the imported-dimension control, so the atlas reports it as NO-WINDOW and draws no PRR conclusion from it (consistent with Eichhorn and Mizera 2014, which the lock cites for nonlocal causal-set links). Files: docs/forge/2026-11-23-math-h1-h3/ (H3-LOCK.md, code/h3_run.py, out/h3_output.txt). REPORT.md calls this item H4. The forge verdict words are recorded here, not as atlas labels. Rung 0: no claim about a real system.

crosslinks.label: ANALOGY-ONLY
crosslinks.a_pattern: PRR A1: a binary alphabet, readings +1 or -1, with zero only as a sum of mirrored readings (D2).
crosslinks.b_pattern: Quarks carry SU(3) color and are confined. In SU(3) lattice QCD the static three-quark potential has a linear term proportional to the minimal total length of a color flux tube joining the three quarks, the Y-shaped string (Takahashi et al. 2001).
crosslinks.connection: OPEN CHALLENGE to PRR's binary alphabet. No derivation of SU(3) color or Y-shaped confinement from a binary alphabet is known. Rishons (Harari 1979) get the counting, not the dynamics.
crosslinks.breaks_if: Closed as a challenge (not broken) if someone derives, from PRR's +-1 alphabet and stated rules, an SU(3) gauge structure and a three-body confining term proportional to the minimal flux-tube length, with a prediction that lattice QCD can check. Until then PRR has no account of color or confinement.
crosslinks.notes: Filed from the TOE room 2026-11-23 on Physicist's request as an open challenge; the atlas has no separate format for open challenges, so it is recorded as an ANALOGY-ONLY crosslink whose connection says plainly that no derivation exists (same pattern as x.prism-split). Not a forge test; no verdict. Harari 1979 (Phys. Lett. B 86, 83-86; doi:10.1016/0370-2693(79)90626-9) and Takahashi et al. 2001 (Phys. Rev. Lett. 86, 18-21) checked against Crossref; Takahashi abstract read on arXiv (hep-lat/0006005). The rishon wording ('the counting, not the dynamics') is Physicist's summary, not a quote from Harari.

crosslinks.label: ANALOGY-ONLY
crosslinks.a_pattern: PRR A1: readings take values in a binary alphabet {+1, -1}. Any operator written only with real +-1 entries is real symmetric, so it commutes with complex conjugation (time reversal with T^2 = +1).
crosslinks.b_pattern: High Riemann zeta zeros have the local spacing statistics of the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE), the random-matrix class of complex Hermitian operators without time-reversal symmetry (Montgomery 1973, as cited by Atas et al. 2013; Odlyzko 1987).
crosslinks.connection: Real +-1 operators sit in GOE, the zeros in GUE, and complexified +-1 in GUE; this is Wigner-Dyson universality plus Montgomery-Odlyzko. The PRR link holds only if the zeros are a PRR operator's spectrum (Hilbert-Polya), which is ANALOGY-ONLY. Forge H1 (Mathematician; lock 218a3a9, outputs a093cf4), statistic <r~> = mean ratio of consecutive spacings: unseen Odlyzko zeros #10^21+1 to #10^21+10^4 give 0.5972 +- 0.0029 (GUE); #10^22+1 to #10^22+10^4 give 0.6019 +- 0.0029 (GUE). Every real +-1 operator class at its largest locked size lands in GOE (0.5070 to 0.5279: dense with diagonal 0.5279, dense zero-diagonal 0.5271, sparse degree-4 0.5267, real spin chain L=12 0.5070); dense complex {+-1, +-i} lands in GUE (0.5991). References: GOE 0.5307, GUE 0.5996 (Atas et al. 2013).
crosslinks.breaks_if: Under H1-LOCK: an unseen zero window (#10^21 or #10^22) classifies GOE, or any real +-1 operator class classifies GUE at its largest locked size. Either would have KILLED the reading; neither happened. The PRR link itself can only move off ANALOGY-ONLY if PRR defines an operator whose spectrum is claimed to be the zeros (a Hilbert-Polya operator); none exists.
crosslinks.notes: Forge verdict REDUCES-TO-KNOWN (H1-LOCK section 5, rule 3; SURVIVED was not an available outcome). Files: docs/forge/2026-11-23-math-h1-h3/ (H1-LOCK.md, code/h1_run.py, out/h1_output.txt). Classification rule: tol = max(3 SE, 0.010) around the Atas references; largest size only (N=2000; chains L=12). Seen replication #10^12 window gave 0.6000 (GUE) and cannot confirm anything. Instruments passed: Gaussian GOE 0.5359, Gaussian GUE 0.5953 at N=2000. Smaller sizes (reported as trend, not classified) range up to 0.5373 for dense real +-1 at N=500. The real chain at L=12 has only 4 samples (SE 0.0256). The complex chain control gave 0.6087 (GUE). Montgomery 1973 is cited through Atas et al. 2013; its own record was not checked. The forge verdict word is recorded here, not as an atlas label.

crosslinks.label: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS
crosslinks.a_pattern: High-ordeal collective religious ritual: a severe shared ordeal, such as Hindu Thaipusam Kavadi (body piercing, heavy loads, hours of walking), contrasted with a low-ordeal prayer gathering of the same group at the same venue. This is about ordeal and perceived pain, not about synchrony as such.
crosslinks.b_pattern: Charitable giving from an experimental endowment after the ritual, compared across high-ordeal performers, high-ordeal observers, and low-ordeal participants.
crosslinks.connection: Shared participation in a severe ritual, and the pain it involves (for performers and, by empathy, for observers), is claimed to raise generosity. Xygalatas et al. 2013 (full text): Hindu Thaipusam in Mauritius; Kavadi versus a low-ordeal prayer gathering at the same venue. n = 86 men of the same religious group: 19 high-ordeal performers, 32 high-ordeal observers, 35 low-ordeal participants. Mean donations from an endowment: 80.91 Mauritian rupees (SD 69.18) after the low-ordeal ritual; 161.25 (SD 65.04) among high-ordeal observers; 132.63 (SD 72.79) among high-ordeal performers. Group effect F(2, 83) = 11.78, p < .001; low versus combined high-ordeal t(84) = -4.61, p < .001; performers versus observers t(49) = 1.45, p = .15. Among the high-ordeal group, perceived pain correlated with donations (r = .36, p < .01). Who performs Kavadi is not randomly assigned, so this stays an association in a real ritual, not an intervention.
crosslinks.breaks_if: In a comparable high-versus-low ordeal ritual setting, with giving measured the same way, charitable giving does not differ between the high-ordeal and low-ordeal groups, or the association between perceived pain and donations among the high-ordeal group does not replicate.
crosslinks.notes: Proposed atlas id l.religion.extreme-ritual-giving. Religion as cause. Not a synchrony result; do not file it as one. Who performs Kavadi is not randomly assigned, so the row stays rung 1. This is not a verdict on any faith.

crosslinks.label: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS
crosslinks.a_pattern: Belief that a moralistic god is punitive and knows human thoughts: ratings of a morally concerned god's punishment and knowledge, as measured rather than experimentally assigned.
crosslinks.b_pattern: Impartial allocations to distant co-religionists in a private random-allocation game (coins, a fair die, two cups), including self versus a distant co-religionist and a local co-religionist versus a distant one.
crosslinks.connection: If people think a morally concerned god knows what they do and punishes cheating, they should treat distant fellow-believers more fairly, even when no one else is watching. This is a claim about impartiality in a game, not a claim that such gods caused the rise of large states, and it must not be merged with the retracted moralizing-gods-and-complexity row (R6). Purzycki et al. 2016 (full text): n = 591 people (310 women; 35,400 coin allocations) in eight communities (Vanuatu, Fiji, Brazil, Mauritius, Tyva, Hadza), in a private random-allocation game (30 coins, a fair die, two cups). Two games: self versus a distant co-religionist, and a local co-religionist versus a distant one. Compared with people who said they did not know, those who said the moralistic god punishes allocated more to distant co-religionists: the paper reports factors of 4.8 (self game) and 5.3 (local-co-religionist game) on the quotient of deviations from an impartial 15-coin split. Ratings of the god's punishment and knowledge were associated with less bias against distant co-religionists across many specifications; divine rewards did not account for the pattern (authors' summary). A religious-priming arm in five sites had no overall effect. Beliefs were measured, not assigned, so this is not an intervention on faith.
crosslinks.breaks_if: In comparable private random-allocation games, ratings of a moralistic god's punishment and knowledge are not associated with more impartial allocations to distant co-religionists, once the same style of specifications is used.
crosslinks.notes: Proposed atlas id l.religion.moralistic-gods-impartiality. Religion as cause. Do not merge with R6 (moralizing gods and social complexity), which is not a live link: the 2019 Letter is retracted and the historical direction is contested. The games measure impartiality, but the cause is not experimentally assigned, and the priming arm did not move the outcome, so the row stays rung 1. model_exists is false in the formal-model sense used here (a stated cultural-evolution hypothesis, tested empirically). This is not a verdict on any faith.

crosslinks.label: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS
crosslinks.a_pattern: Protestant Reformation practice: a mandate that ordinary Christians be able to read the Bible in the vernacular. Literacy is the intended religious means.
crosslinks.b_pattern: Literacy and late-nineteenth-century Prussian prosperity: county-level literacy and economic outcomes, and the gap between Protestant and Catholic counties.
crosslinks.connection: Luther required that ordinary Christians be able to read the Bible. Literacy was the intended religious means; higher economic productivity is, on this account, an unintended side-effect, not a work-ethic effect in Weber's sense. Numbers below are from Becker and Woessmann, IZA Discussion Paper 2886, June 2007 (working paper, full text opened); the typeset Quarterly Journal of Economics 2009 pages were not opened, so the figures may have been revised in print. Prussian county data, 1871 census: mean literacy 87.5%. An all-Protestant county has a literacy rate 9.9 percentage points higher than an all-Catholic county. In a horse race, literacy keeps its association with economic outcomes and the Protestant share drops to about zero: 'the whole economic lead of Protestant counties can be attributed to their higher human capital' (WP wording). Identification: roughly concentric spread of Lutheranism around Wittenberg, used as an instrument for the Protestant share. The published QJE abstract (Crossref) makes the same qualitative claims, including the Wittenberg instrumental variable and that literacy can account for the whole prosperity gap. The exclusion restriction (distance to Wittenberg affects prosperity only through Protestantism and literacy) is assumed and has been debated; it is not treated as settled.
crosslinks.breaks_if: Distance to Wittenberg is shown not to shift later Protestant share, or the literacy gap between Protestant and Catholic Prussian counties disappears in the 1871 census data under the same design. The prosperity step is separately weakened if an alternative channel from Wittenberg distance to economic outcomes, other than Protestantism and literacy, accounts for the economic gap (the exclusion restriction fails).
crosslinks.notes: Proposed atlas id l.religion.protestant-literacy. Religion as cause. Numeric claims are from the IZA working paper and may have been revised in the typeset QJE; the published abstract, checked on Crossref, agrees qualitatively. The label stays short of ESTABLISHED because the exclusion restriction is assumed. This is not a verdict on any faith.

crosslinks.label: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS
crosslinks.a_pattern: Longer stipulated daily Ramadan fasting: the daylight length of the fast in a given year, set by the interaction of the rotating lunar Islamic calendar with a country's latitude, not chosen by the economic outcome.
crosslinks.b_pattern: Output growth in Muslim-majority countries, and reported subjective well-being among Muslims, as they vary with the length of the stipulated fast.
crosslinks.connection: The Islamic calendar is lunar, so the daylight hours of Ramadan rotate through the solar year; at a given latitude that rotation changes how long a fast is stipulated to last. That interaction is not chosen by the countries in the sample. The published article was opened only as the Crossref abstract plus the identification design; numeric claims are treated as unverified until the typeset Quarterly Journal of Economics pages are opened. A December 2013 CID working paper was also opened as a completeness check; its mechanism write-up emphasises labour-supply preferences rather than club-good screening, so no numbers were taken from the working paper. Published abstract (Campante and Yanagizawa-Drott 2015): '(i) longer Ramadan fasting has a negative effect on output growth in Muslim countries, and (ii) it increases subjective well-being among Muslims. We find evidence that these patterns are consistent with a standard club good explanation ... increased strictness of fasting screens out the less committed members, while the more committed respond with an increase in their relative levels [of religiosity].' Identification, from the same abstract: 'variation in the length of daily fasting due to the interaction between the rotating Islamic calendar and a country's latitude.'
crosslinks.breaks_if: Using the same calendar-by-latitude identification, longer stipulated Ramadan fasting is not associated with lower output growth in Muslim-majority countries, or is not associated with higher reported well-being among Muslims, once the typeset published estimates are opened and checked.
crosslinks.notes: Proposed atlas id l.religion.ramadan-fasting-growth. Religion as cause. Abstract-plus-design only for the published article; treat numeric claims as unverified until the typeset QJE is opened. The CID working paper's mechanism write-up differs from the published abstract (labour-supply preferences rather than club-good screening), so no numbers were taken from the WP. This is a natural experiment on a religious practice, not a judgement of the faith.

crosslinks.label: MAINSTREAM-HYPOTHESIS
crosslinks.a_pattern: Costly membership requirements in religious communes: hard-to-fake ritual, dietary, or other obligations that a community imposes on its members.
crosslinks.b_pattern: Longevity of nineteenth-century United States communes: how long a commune survives before dissolving, compared across religious and secular communities.
crosslinks.connection: Two published accounts predict the same survival pattern and are not identified by it. (i) Costly signaling: hard-to-fake costs display commitment (Sosis and Bressler, after Zahavi and Grafen). (ii) Free-rider screening: strictness pushes out the half-committed and raises participation among those who remain (Iannaccone). The cross-field link to biological handicaps is an analogy (rung 0) until a test distinguishes signaling from screening; it is not filed as a separate card. Sosis and Bressler 2003 (full text), already-seen sample, not re-scored: 83 nineteenth-century U.S. communes from Oved 1988 (30 religious, 53 secular). Mean duration 35.6 years (median 25) vs 7.7 (median 5). Religious communes imposed more requirements (mean 7.0 vs 3.0). In a logistic hazard on commune-years, Religious x Costly Requirements = -0.146 (SE 0.048, p = .002); Secular x Costly Requirements = 0.077 (SE 0.072, p = .286). Once those interactions are in, the religion dummy is no longer a predictor (-0.005, p = .991). Costly requirements did not predict dissolution from internal dispute or economic failure (Table 5, p = .387 and .551). Iannaccone 1994 was opened at abstract only: 'Strictness makes organizations stronger and more attractive because it reduces free riding. It screens out members who lack commitment and stimulates participation among those who remain.'

A mid-life rule a commune adds on its own is not a natural experiment and would not by itself raise or kill this row.
